messages.author: David Poole
messages.body:
Hello everybody,
I was wondering about the status of pysander. I was working on making some
nice automation with pytraj, but when it got to running esander, it
complained I needed to import the sander module. Lo, when I tried this it
failed. I checked the pytraj documentation but following the advice there
to install by conda--the module simply wasn't found. I checked the pysander
documentation (
https://github.com/Amber-MD/pysander
) but this leads to a
404.
So is pysander available? If so, please let me know how to load its module
and maybe we can update the documentation for this...somewhere?
Also, for pytraj folks, is there documentation for using lie in pytraj? it
currently just says LIE which isn't very helpful unless you have some
strong and serious doubts about the method.
Kindly,
David P.

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Fri, Mar 18, 2022, David Poole wrote:
>
>So is pysander available? If so, please let me know how to load its module
>and maybe we can update the documentation for this...somewhere?
Pysander is available within AmberTools. (But it's possible that it was not
correctly built -- We'd need to know details then.)
Note that pysander is not an executable program, just an extension module
named "sander".
Thanks for the note about the github page -- that needs a thorough cleanup.
...good luck....dac

Hi David P.,
Just like Dave said, if you installed AmberTools, you should have pysander
(and in python code, you can 'import sander').
>

For pytraj, there is no document except the help message.
For detail document, you need to look at cpptraj manual:
https://amberhub.chpc.utah.edu/lie/
Hai

messages.author: David Poole
messages.body:
I found success in getting it installed using conda forge independently of
my amber/ambertools installation. I am unsure why it didn't work off the
bat as parmed.py and pytraj both worked (mostly), and even pamred.py
allowed me to use esander. I think it was just a matter of the version
included in ambertools?
If there are opportunities to help clean up github documentation, maybe the
community could help more as well? That might be a good thing to push as
well.
Alas now that things are working, I have a bug to report: While I can use
esander in pytraj to do gb (igb > 0) and pme calculations, when I attempt
to do two or pb calculations (ipb > 0 or igb = 10), I get a
segmentation fault from pb_init() and the program exits. The minimum
example is computing the single point pb for any two loaded structures in
pytraj. Calculations can be set up with either mm_options (options.ipb > 0,
or igb = 10) or by setting igb in the esander method (igb = 10), which all
lead to the same result. This would be particularly useful for my new
workflows for mmxbsa calculations using the pytraj interface.
Kindly,
David
